## 1. The Rust engine core (`src/rust`)

State. Zero-dependency, Apache-2.0-certified KL-NMF kernel; hand-rolled
scalar GEMM with fixed ascending-s accumulation (the frozen numerics
contract, `src/rust/src/replicates.rs:32-34`); the L1-L5 memory-structure
phase landed and measured 1.223x (step core) / 1.107x (end-to-end) on the
m1s fixture (p11 devlog, differential twin microbench). The system-level
parity row stands at a 13.4-72.9x breach across the O5 147-cell grid
(~6.7x needed).

Findings.

- (1a, performance, decisive) The breach is NOT hand-rolled-vs-BLAS: the
  faer probe (`/tmp/faer-probe`, 2026-11-28) measured the same four-pass
  KL structure through faer 0.24.4 at 1.31x (96x1000) and 1.20x
  (96x4000) over the scalar twin — the skinny products (96x10
  transposes) and elementwise ratio passes deny BLAS-class kernels their
  arena. The hypothesis "swap the library, close the gap" is refuted by
  measurement; the bit-identity wall stays up (its price would have been
  one re-anchoring — faer is bit-identical run-to-run and across
  Seq/rayon(4) — but 1.3x does not buy the wall's removal).
- (1b, performance, decisive) With the library swap refuted and the
  GEMM-microkernel door closed at bit-identity (p11 probe: hand-SIMD
  1.02x), the ONLY remaining levers are (i) in-fit parallelism (L6,
  user-blessed 2026-11-27, unimplemented) and (ii) work-volume reduction
  in the iteration protocol itself. Which of these holds the ~6.7x is an
  OPEN empirical question — the O5 gap decomposition (kernel time vs
  work volume vs shape mix) is the single most valuable missing number
  in the project.
- (1c, engineering) L6 requires amending the concurrency law
  (replicates.rs module docs + architecture.qmd contracts 6+7). The p11
  proof sketch (j-disjoint accumulation) is NOT automatically
  transferable to j-splitting; the deciding evidence is the
  thread-count bit-identity gate on all guarded workloads, not the
  sketch.
- (1d, accuracy) Accuracy posture is sound: accuracy non-regression
  travels with every change; the anchors are bit-pinned; the tolerance
  re-anchoring option stays declined by user ruling (2026-11-27).

Tasks: T-1 (O5 gap decomposition, P1, read-only), T-2 (L6 design memo,
P2 prose-now; implementation gated on G0 resume), T-3 (work-volume
algorithm lane — early-stopping / convergence budgets / initialization
quality — P2, scoped by T-1's outcome).

## 4. The test/law system (`tests/testthat`, `bench/scenarios`)

State. 116 test files; the CS-1..21 witness series with byte-frozen
clause/class/label ledgers; 22 scenario drivers each ending in its own
verdict line; the 580-expectation touched-law battery green this
session; CS-21 landed with 10 units / 275 expectations / byte-stable
witnesses.

Findings.

- (4a, engineering) The witness ledgers freeze float-derived bytes
  (cluster vectors, relabel indices). Those bytes are platform-stable
  only because the kernel is bit-identical; a future wall decision would
  force a census-posture migration across the series. Archived, not a
  task today.
- (4b, engineering, live) Scenario laws skip under R CMD check
  (.ms_root Built: discriminator). Correct by design, but it means the
  cran-shape monolith (§5b) runs an UNPRICED door: its test phase costs
  69 min observed while the sharded lane prices the same suite around
  25 min. The pricing model has a blind spot the shard tables cannot
  see.

Tasks: T-4 (add the monolith door to the pricing story when T-2 lands:
either the ratcheted timer carries a dated note, or the monolith's
test-phase cost gets its own measured line), no other open items.

## 5. CI and governance (`.github/workflows`, `tools/ci`)

State. Sharded check lanes with attested budgets; the fail-closed
attestation census (2026-10-24 law); the pin law family (S7@0.2.2 per
#118, covr@3.6.5 per #141); the extras snapshot fix (#137) verified
EXTRAS-ATTEST both-ok on the live test.

Open defects, evidence-cited.

- (5a) coverage leg: the covr pin WORKED for its target class (covr
  3.6.5 installed, llvm-cov death class gone, EXTRAS both ok — run
  46012520485) but shard 4 still dies `covr-failed` under 3.6.5 with
  `Failure in msuiter-tests/testthat.Rout.fail` (fragments:
  "Not yet available:" + "_bundled())") — a REAL test failure under
  instrumentation, independent of the 4.0.0 float. The full shard log is
  lost because `covr-logs/` is never uploaded as an artifact (the
  transcripts group carries tail-25 only). Repair: (i) add a
  failure-only `covr-logs` artifact upload step; (ii) re-dispatch and
  read the actual Rout.fail; (iii) fix the failing test or its
  instrumentation-only environment gap.
- (5b) cran-shape-check: both OS legs die AT the 90-minute timeout
  (14:04->15:34 on 2026-11-27; same class the night before), with the
  test phase 69 min in at kill time. Drift evidence: the last-green run
  (43590958442, 2026-11-14) ran the ubuntu leg in 64m00s — the monolith
  grew >=26 min across the CS-17..21 + G0-law-file landings. Repair:
  the coverage-lineage-style ratchet 90->120 with a dated comment and
  this drift witness; then answer why the monolith's test phase triples
  the sharded pricing (T-4).
- (5c) test-heavy is needs-chained to coverage (`:603`) and cancels with
  it; the version-fanout devel leg's failure is the known
  continue-on-error advisory class (S7 x R-devel upstream) — no action,
  documented so it never reads as a new defect.

Tasks: T-5 (covr diagnosability upload + shard-4 adjudication, P1),
T-6 (cran-shape ratchet 90->120 PR with the drift witness, P1).
